stem: In triangle \(PQR\), \(PQ = PR = 25\) and \(QR = 40\). What is the value of \(\sin P\)?
solution: The altitude from \(P\) bisects \(\overline{QR}\), so it has length \(\sqrt{25^{2} - 20^{2}} = 15\), and the area is \(\frac{1}{2}(40)(15) = 300\).
The area also equals \(\frac{1}{2}(PQ)(PR)\sin P = \frac{1}{2}(25)(25)\sin P\).
\(\frac{625}{2}\sin P = 300\), so \(\sin P = \frac{600}{625} = \frac{24}{25}\). (Angle \(P\) is obtuse, so this differs from the sine of either half of angle \(P\).)

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the size of \(\cos P = -\frac{7}{25}\) (law of cosines), not \(\sin P\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\sin Q = \frac{15}{25}\), the sine of a base angle, not of angle \(P\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{20}{25}\), the sine of half of angle \(P\); the work stops before finding the sine of the whole angle.
explanation.D: Correct. Computing the area two ways gives \(\frac{625}{2}\sin P = 300\), so \(\sin P = \frac{24}{25}\).

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert d('P','Q')==25 and d('P','R')==25 and d('Q','R')==40
cP=Rational(25**2+25**2-40**2,2*25*25)
ans=sqrt(1-cP**2)
assert abs(N(sin(ang('Q','P','R')*pi/180))-ans)<1e-3
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==Rational(24,25)
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
